title: Registry study for the identification of patients with hereditary alpha tryptasemia
summary:
Hereditary Alpha Tryptasemia (HαT) is a genetic condition that is passed down in families (autosomal dominant). So far, not much is known about how common it is or what symptoms it causes. People with HαT often have slightly increased or high levels of an enzyme in their blood called tryptase. Tryptase comes from mast cells, which are part of the immune system and play a role in allergic reactions.
HαT is found more often in people with certain conditions, such as systemic mastocytosis or those who have had a severe allergic reaction to insect stings.
In addition, HαT may be linked to a range of other symptoms. These can include skin rashes like hives, itching, sensitivities to certain foods or medications, irritable bowel symptoms, trouble with focus or mood, and unusually flexible joints (hypermobility).

interventions.name: Patients who were tested for HαT due to elevated tryptase levels and/or typical symptoms

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Submission of a blood sample
- Written consent for inclusion in the registry
- The ability to understand and complete the questionnaire
Exclusion criteria:
- Decline of registry participation
